Member (Gurpreet Martin): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Gurpreet Martin, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Gurpreet Martin): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Gurpreet Martin): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Gurpreet Martin): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Gurpreet Martin): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Gurpreet Martin): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Gurpreet Martin): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Member (Gurpreet Martin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Gurpreet Martin): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Gurpreet Martin): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Member (Gurpreet Martin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.
SL-000034.narrative_summary: Gurpreet Martin, a Sun Life member, contacted support on a declined claim case. Agent Ryan MacDonald compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet. In the end, it was resolved on this interaction, and the member rated it CSAT 4 (satisfied).

SL-000048.transcript:
Member (Mei Singh): My medication claim was put on hold for more information and I don't know what you need.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Mei Singh, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mei Singh): My doctor charges 45 dollars to fill in forms.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Mei Singh): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Mei Singh): I uploaded the prescription through the app already.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which medication or service is the request about?
Member (Mei Singh): A new medication my specialist started me on last week.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the pharmacy give you the name of the form they need?
Member (Mei Singh): They said 'prior authorization' and gave me a number to call. That's it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which pharmacy are you using?
Member (Mei Singh): The one near my work. They said they can resubmit as soon as it's approved.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Is your doctor's office aware a form is needed?
Member (Mei Singh): I told them, and they said they'd need the form itself from Sun Life.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've checked the information request and the documents already on file.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): For this medication the plan needs a prior authorization from your doctor, not just the prescription.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I'm checking whether anything from your doctor's office is already on file.
Member (Mei Singh): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The drug is on the prior authorization list, so we need the completed form from your doctor before it can be covered. I've emailed you the form and noted that you're waiting on it.
Member (Mei Singh): And I'm paying the doctor for the form on top of everything.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I understand. Keep the receipt for the form, and I'll note on your file how much medication you have left.
Member (Mei Singh): How long does the review take once it's in?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Usually two to three business days. I've asked for it to be prioritised given your supply.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: the form is in your email, your doctor completes and faxes it, and the review usually takes two to three business days.
Member (Mei Singh): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Mathieu Wilson): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Mathieu Wilson, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mathieu Wilson): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Mathieu Wilson): Yes, that's right.
Member (Mathieu Wilson): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Mathieu Wilson): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Mathieu Wilson): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Mathieu Wilson): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Mathieu Wilson): They said they billed it the same way as always.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Mathieu Wilson): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Mathieu Wilson): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Mathieu Wilson): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Mathieu Wilson): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-000317.transcript:
Member (Hannah Morrison): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Hannah Morrison, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Hannah Morrison): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Hannah Morrison): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Hannah Morrison): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Hannah Morrison): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Hannah Morrison): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Hannah Morrison): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Hannah Morrison): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Hannah Morrison): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Hannah Morrison): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Hannah Morrison): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Hannah Morrison): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Until that form arrives, the funds stay invested in your current options, so they've moved with the market.
Member (Owen Fortin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer form from the receiving institution. I can't release it until that arrives, but I've sent them a reminder.
Member (Owen Fortin): So I've lost money because of a form nobody told me about?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I understand. I've noted on your file that you've been waiting since June, so it's visible if this needs a review.
Member (Owen Fortin): Who follows up?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Retirement services will. I've asked them to call you once the form arrives.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): To recap: we're waiting on your bank's signed form, a reminder has gone to them today, and retirement services will call you when it's in.
Member (Owen Fortin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Leila Roy): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Hi Leila Roy, Daniel Okafor here — let me pull that up.
Member (Leila Roy): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Leila Roy): The member ID is on the welcome letter.
Member (Leila Roy): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Leila Roy): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Did the letter mention any documents that were missing?
Member (Leila Roy): No, just that it doesn't meet the criteria.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Has the dental office called us about this directly?
Member (Leila Roy): They said they called and got the same answer as me.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Are you in any pain right now?

Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): The assessment is done against the plan's criteria for crowns, which are set by Health Canada.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I'm looking at the latest assessment on your file now.
Member (Leila Roy): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): The first request was missing the radiograph date. The second one is complete and has been assessed, and it's approved. Your dentist will get the confirmation today.
Member (Leila Roy): So the crown is covered now?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Yes. It's approved at your plan's coverage level, and your dentist will get the confirmation today.
Member (Leila Roy): Do I pay anything?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): That depends on your co-payment level. Your dentist will see it on the confirmation.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): To recap: the crown is approved, and your dentist will get the confirmation today with your co-payment.
Member (Leila Roy): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Liam Patel): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Liam Patel, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Liam Patel): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Liam Patel): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Liam Patel): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Owen Wilson): My pension transfer has been sitting for months and my bank says they're waiting on you.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Hi Owen Wilson, Marc Tremblay here — let me pull that up.
Member (Owen Wilson): The receiving institution says they never got anything.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Owen Wilson): Yes, that's right.
Member (Owen Wilson): The market's moved since then and I've lost money waiting.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Which plan is the transfer from?
Member (Owen Wilson): My old employer's pension plan. I left the company in May.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Where is the money going?
Member (Owen Wilson): To an RRSP at my bank. They say they're waiting on Sun Life.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Did the bank send you a transfer form to sign as well?
Member (Owen Wilson): I think so. They handled their side.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Let me take a look. I've traced the transfer request and the paperwork on the plan account.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Your request came in on June 14. The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer authorization from the receiving institution, which is standard for locked-in pension money.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Until that form arrives, the funds stay invested in your current options, so they've moved with the market.
Member (Owen Wilson): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): The transfer was held because the receiving institution's form wasn't signed. It came in this morning, so I've released it, and the funds will move within five business days.
Member (Owen Wilson): So it's finally moving?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Yes. The form arrived this morning, and I've released the transfer.
Member (Owen Wilson): How long until my bank has it?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Usually five business days, and you'll get a confirmation letter from us.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): So the transfer is released and should reach your bank within five business days.
Member (Owen Wilson): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-001209.transcript:
Member (Leila Patel): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Leila Patel, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Leila Patel): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Leila Patel): The member ID is on the welcome letter.
Member (Leila Patel): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Leila Patel): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the letter mention any documents that were missing?
Member (Leila Patel): No, just that it doesn't meet the criteria.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has the dental office called us about this directly?
Member (Leila Patel): They said they called and got the same answer as me.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Are you in any pain right now?

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I'm looking at the latest assessment on your file now.
Member (Leila Patel): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The decision follows the plan criteria set by Health Canada, and I don't have a more specific reason on my screen. Your dentist can submit a new request with more clinical notes, and I've noted that you asked for the reason.
Member (Leila Patel): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Leila Patel): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Leila Patel): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Hannah Cote): I've been off work for six weeks and still haven't had a decision on my short-term disability claim.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Hannah Cote, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Hannah Cote): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Hannah Cote): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Hannah Cote): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): When did you go off work?
Member (Hannah Cote): Six weeks ago. I submitted my part in the first week.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?
Member (Hannah Cote): They said about three weeks ago, but I haven't seen anything confirming it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Have you been contacted by a case manager yet?
Member (Hannah Cote): Not that I know of. Nobody has called me.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Are you receiving any other income right now, like sick days from work?
Member (Hannah Cote): My sick days ran out two weeks ago.

Agent (Priya Sandhu): I know that's hard. I've marked the file as a priority because you have no other income right now.
Member (Hannah Cote): Is there anything I can do to speed it up?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Ask HR for the date they sent the statement. If it's missing, that's the one thing holding the file.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: the file is waiting on the employer's statement, your case manager has been asked to call you, and I've noted your preferred contact times.
Member (Hannah Cote): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-001230.transcript:
Member (Owen Cote): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Owen Cote, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.
Member (Owen Cote): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Owen Cote): Yes, that's right.
Member (Owen Cote): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Owen Cote): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Owen Cote): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Owen Cote): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Owen Cote): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Owen Cote): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Owen Cote): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Owen Cote): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Olivia Kim): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Olivia Kim, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.
Member (Olivia Kim): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Olivia Kim): Yes, that's right.
Member (Olivia Kim): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Olivia Kim): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Olivia Kim): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Olivia Kim): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Olivia Kim): They said they billed it the same way as always.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Olivia Kim): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Olivia Kim): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Olivia Kim): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Olivia Kim): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Jasmine Wong): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Noah Chen): I'm waiting on a decision on my disability claim and nobody has called me.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Hi Noah Chen, Daniel Okafor here — let me pull that up.
Member (Noah Chen): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Noah Chen): Yes, that's right.
Member (Noah Chen): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): When did you go off work?
Member (Noah Chen): Six weeks ago. I submitted my part in the first week.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Have you been contacted by a case manager yet?
Member (Noah Chen): Not that I know of. Nobody has called me.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Is there a good number and time to reach you?
Member (Noah Chen): My mobile, any time before three. I have appointments in the afternoons.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Are you receiving any other income right now, like sick days from work?
Member (Noah Chen): My sick days ran out two weeks ago.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the disability file and the case manager's task list.

Agent (Daniel Okafor): Your file has your statement and your doctor's statement. I'm checking whether the employer's statement has come in.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Once the file is complete, the case manager makes the decision and calls you to explain it.

Member (Noah Chen): Is there anything I can do to speed it up?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Ask HR for the date they sent the statement. If it's missing, that's the one thing holding the file.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): To recap: the file is waiting on the employer's statement, your case manager has been asked to call you, and I've noted your preferred contact times.
Member (Noah Chen): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Chantal Ahmed): I'm waiting on a decision on my disability claim and nobody has called me.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Chantal Ahmed, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Chantal Ahmed): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Chantal Ahmed): Yes, that's right.
Member (Chantal Ahmed): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?
Member (Chantal Ahmed): They said about three weeks ago, but I haven't seen anything confirming it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Have you been contacted by a case manager yet?
Member (Chantal Ahmed): Not that I know of. Nobody has called me.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Is there a good number and time to reach you?
Member (Chantal Ahmed): My mobile, any time before three. I have appointments in the afternoons.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Are you receiving any other income right now, like sick days from work?

Member (Chantal Ahmed): So I'm still waiting with no income?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I know that's hard. I've marked the file as a priority because you have no other income right now.
Member (Chantal Ahmed): Is there anything I can do to speed it up?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Ask HR for the date they sent the statement. If it's missing, that's the one thing holding the file.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: the file is waiting on the employer's statement, your case manager has been asked to call you, and I've noted your preferred contact times.
Member (Chantal Ahmed): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Noah Roy): My son needs braces and I want to know what my plan pays before we commit.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Hi Noah Roy, Daniel Okafor here — let me pull that up.
Member (Noah Roy): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Happy to check that for you.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Noah Roy): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Noah Roy): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Is he listed as a dependant on your plan?
Member (Noah Roy): Yes, since he was born.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?
Member (Noah Roy): They gave me an estimate of about six thousand dollars.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?
Member (Noah Roy): No, this is the first time.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Is the orthodontist here in Canada?
Member (Noah Roy): Yes, here in town.

Agent (Daniel Okafor): Orthodontic coverage depends on your employer's plan, so I'm checking your certificate now.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.
Member (Noah Roy): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Orthodontics is covered at 50% up to a 2,500-dollar lifetime maximum for dependants under 19. I recommend a pre-determination first, and I've emailed you the steps.
Member (Noah Roy): What's a pre-determination?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): The orthodontist sends the treatment plan first, and we confirm exactly what's covered before any work starts.
Member (Noah Roy): Great, that helps.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): So, 50% up to 2,500 dollars, a pre-determination first, and your spouse's plan can cover part of the rest.
Member (Noah Roy): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): To recap: we're waiting on your bank's signed form, a reminder has gone to them today, and retirement services will call you when it's in.
Member (Liam Martin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Liam Martin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Olivia Singh): How much would a lower amount cost?

Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Noah Wilson, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Noah Wilson): My spouse has coverage through her work too.

Agent (Sophie Belanger): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?

Member (Noah Wilson): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Is he listed as a dependant on your plan?

Agent (Sophie Belanger): How old is he?

Member (Noah Wilson): How would I check that?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): It would show under Accounts in the app. I don't see one on your certificate, but HR can confirm.

Member (Noah Chen): I'm following up again — my dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Noah Chen, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Noah Chen): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Noah Chen): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Noah Chen): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Noah Chen): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Noah Chen): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Noah Chen): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Noah Chen): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Noah Chen): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Noah Chen): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Noah Chen): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Noah Chen): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Noah Chen): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.

Member (Chantal Ahmed): I'm following up again — my dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Chantal Ahmed, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Chantal Ahmed): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Chantal Ahmed): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.

Agent (Sophie Belanger): Is this the first request or a resubmission?

Agent (Sophie Belanger): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.

Agent (Sophie Belanger): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.

Agent (Sophie Belanger): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.
